text:
maya: Heads-up — we had a weird tail-latency incident on eu-west GPUs around 02:30 UTC. Not a full OOM or preempt, but ~30% of requests to shared pools hit 2-3s tails.
alex: saw similar blips in metrics — kernel stalls on a subset of cards, appears correlated with mixed fp16/int8 workloads on the same host.
liam: that's the heterogenous-bins packing again. Some tenants run full-precision debugging jobs that thrash GPU memory bandwidth.
maya: thinking out loud: instead of blacklisting tenants or hard-evicting, can we route traffic to a "compatibility bin" that forces model variant fallback (quantized or smaller seq) when probe detects bandwidth contention? like a graceful degradation path.
alex: +1 for graceful fallbacks. We already have model-variant routing but it's coarse. Could we add a short-lived routing tag that signals "low-bandwidth-mode" for the tenant? then runtime picks quantized kernel.
liam: rough config idea:

```
route_policy:
  name: low_bw_fallback
  triggers:
    - host.pci_bandwidth_util > 0.85 for 30s
  action:
    - annotate_request: runtime_hint=quantized_low_bw
    - divert_to_pool: compat-quantized-bins (ttl=60s)
```

maya: exactly. TTL needs to be short to avoid throughput loss. Also need cost accounting — we should attribute extra cost when we divert to dedicated compat bins so billing + SLO teams are aware.
infra-bot: detected: host-group eu-west-3a bandwidth spike at 2045689000. Auto-sample of affected requests captured.
sre-oncall: main questions — how do fallbacks interact with canary/AB rollouts? and what if model quality regresses under quantized fallback?
alex: we'll add a deterministic switch: only route to fallback if tenant has an approved fallback bundle. That avoids accidental quality surprises. We can tie it to the model catalog: model.variant.allow_low_bw = true.
liam: for rollouts, fallback routing should be transparent to A/B: traffic keep same allocation but with metric tag so evals can surface quality drift. Add an automatic eval trigger when more than 5% of requests use fallback for 10m.
maya: good. For implementation, runtime needs two quick things: 1) a cheap host-local probe for sustained pci/bandwidth contention, and 2) very fast request annotation path (no extra remote calls). We can reuse existing eBPF NIC probes for #1 and the request router already supports annotations.
sre-oncall: propose we pilot in eu-west on a few low-risk tenants for 48h. I'll coordinate with support to pre-warn customers and enable rollback flags.
alex: I'll prototype the routing policy and add feature-flag gating. Also adding a metric: fallback_rate_by_tenant, fallback_p99_latency, quality_regression_alert.
maya: thanks. Can someone open a lightweight RFC (1-pager) that captures flow, billing implications, and a safety checklist (approved fallbacks, rollback, eval hooks)? tagging @liam for draft.
liam: on it. Will post draft in #eng-infra/rfcs by EOD and include a simple test plan.
maya: sweet. If pilot looks good we can fold into autoscaling policies as a cheaper mitigation vs burst capacity.
alex: :thumbsup:
infra-bot: note: scheduled job to collect fallback usage metrics will run at 2045692600.
